title: Compact polyglot bootstraps & cookbook recipes for SDK streaming + retry ergonomics
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a small set of 'bento' starter templates and cookbook snippets that demonstrate best-practice usage of the Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) focused on streaming ergonomics, robust retry policies, and compact deployable examples.

Scope:
- Four leaf templates: Next.js (Edge + streaming incremental hydration), FastAPI (server-sent events and background KV cache usage), idiomatic Go HTTP server (single-file bootstrap with graceful shutdown and streaming), and a cross-platform CLI shim (Python or Go) illustrating resumable streaming and idempotent retries.
- Each template must be intentionally compact (<= ~200 lines core example) and include a README, minimal CI job, and one integration-level smoke test.
- Provide cookbook snippets for: retry policy DSL examples (exponential backoff with jitter + idempotency key), client-side backpressure and cancellation hooks, prefix/KV cache usage, and structured output parsing patterns.

Non-goals: Full production-grade deployment manifests for every cloud provider (we'll link to Dedicated/Private docs instead). Large sample datasets or long-running demo infra.

Deliverables:
- Next.js example using streaming SSR (Edge) with token-level telemetry stub and sample prompt set.
- FastAPI example showing SSE generator that yields partial payloads and resumes after transient errors using idempotency keys.
- Go HTTP server single-file blueprint demonstrating graceful shutdown, KV cache hot-path, and streaming to clients with context cancellation.
- CLI example showing resumable downloads of streamed completions and an ergonomics helper that wraps retry policies.
- Cookbook.md with 6 compact snippets: retry patterns, streaming backpressure, structured-output extraction, batching examples, simple evaluation harness for starter prompts, and cost-saving quantization recommendation note.

Acceptance criteria:
- All templates build and run locally via README steps on macOS/Linux.
- Each repo has one automated smoke test in CI that runs a short local runtime mock (or uses a test token) and validates streaming payload and retry logic.
- Code uses the SDK public APIs (no private/internal-only helpers) and demonstrates streaming callback patterns, retry helper usage, and cancellation tokens.
- Templates are reviewed by SDK lead and docs to ensure examples are idiomatic and small enough for copy/paste.

Notes on implementation: prefer minimal dependencies, prefer stdlib for Go and minimal frameworks for Python (FastAPI) and TS (Next.js). Use a single configuration file pattern for the examples to show how to swap from hosted to dedicated/private endpoints. Include a short telemetry snippet that emits token counts to STDOUT to help users understand cost implications.
acceptance_criteria: Next.js example streams via Edge and completes end-to-end with sample prompt set
FastAPI SSE example yields partial chunks and can resume after a simulated transient failure
Go HTTP server example demonstrates graceful shutdown and context cancellation handling while streaming
CLI example can resume a partially downloaded streamed completion using an idempotency key
Each template includes README, one CI smoke test, and <= ~200 lines for core example
SDK APIs used are public and demonstrate retry helper, streaming callbacks, and structured output parsing
